name: british-thriller-trailer-braams
style: British voices, London crime-drama trailer, UK telly thriller cut. Shouted English speech, not singing. Metronomic clock tick and a noise riser swelling beneath panicked East End paramedics. A single enormous low braam lands with a falling sub, slamming the momentum to a halt. A thin, reedy, plummy toff shrieks a spoilt tantrum behind a car window. Pitched riser climbing again, ending on one long cardiac monitor whine, then nothing at all.
exclude: American accent, US accent, Hollywood, epic orchestra, choir, singing, sung chorus, melodic vocal, rap, cheerful, comedy, trailer voiceover, fade out
lyrics:
[Intro: steady clock tick, noise riser swelling, siren hissing through rain]
[Spoken, screamed: Essex woman, paramedic, desperate]
Sixty over thirty! Fucking hurry up, we're gonna lose him!
[Spoken, shouted: Cockney man, paramedic, out of breath]
Sats dropping, he's peri-arrest!
[Spoken, bellowed: Cockney driver, furious at the traffic]
Two minutes out! Get the fuck out of the way!
[Massive braam, sub falls away, the ambulance halts]
[Spoken: Cockney man, stunned]
Why have we stopped?!
[Spoken, through car glass but loud: reedy, nasal, plummy English toff, spoilt schoolboy tantrum]
I said raspberry-shaped hors d'oeuvres!
[Pitched riser climbing, monitor beeps slowing]
[Spoken, hushed: Essex woman, almost inaudible]
Fifty over twen—
[Monitor flatline, the last hit]
[Nothing]
[End]
